To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we develop a new algorithm that uses bidirectional compression to achieve the same convergence rate of algorithms using only up-link (from local workers to central server) compression, and our analysis is based on a precise control of the perturbation on the local models.

(1) we propose a new algorithm that combines bidirectional compression with model compression; (2) the proposed algorithm achieves the same convergence guarantees as algorithms using only unidirectional compression; and (3) we develop a new analysis to prove the convergence of the proposed algorithm

(i) the proposed method, MCM, is the first method that achieves the same rate of convergence as algorithms with only uplink compression, (ii) MCM can handle a wide variety of compression operators, (iii) the analysis of the proposed method is more challenging than previous methods due to the perturbation of the local models and (iv) the analysis can be extended to incorporate worker dependent compression operators and partial participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new algorithm that improves the communication efficiency of distributed learning, while maintaining the same convergence guarantees as previous algorithms.
the design of a novel compression scheme for a distributed setting.
a new algorithmic approach to preserve the global model in a distributed learning setting with a central server, and we provide a rigorous analysis of its convergence rate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose an algorithm that achieves the best of both worlds: it preserves the central model and performs downlink compression, which is faster than uplink compression.
MCM is the first algorithm that achieves a convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}\left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\right)$ in a distributed setting using only uplink compression.
we develop a new approach that enables bidirectional communication in a distributed learning setting, while achieving the same convergence rates as algorithms using only the uplink compression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MCM achieves the same convergence rates of previous algorithms using only uplinks while using bidirectional compression.
we provide a new approach to deal with communication constraints in a decentralized setting.
we provide a new approach to preserve the model on the central server and use it for faster convergence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preserving the global model can be beneficial for distributed learning.
the central server does not need to perform downlink compression to achieve the same rate as if it had access to the full gradients.
preserving the global model is key to achieve fast convergence rates with bidirectional compression.
